title: 5.6 A Power-Efficient CORDIC-Less Digital Polar Transmitter Using 1b DSM-Based PA Supporting 256-QAM
problem: Digital polar transmitters require CORDIC for I/Q-to-polar conversion but CORDIC's nonlinearity causes bandwidth expansion of AM/PM outputs, challenging wideband implementations. Switched-capacitor PAs suffer low efficiency at power backoff; existing AM/PM modulation methods (PI, DTC, VMD SCPA) introduce further nonlinearity requiring complex DPD.
motivation: High data-rate digital transmitters must support wide baseband bandwidths; conventional CORDIC-based polar architecture becomes impractical as bandwidth increases, demanding alternative modulation approaches.
method: The transmitter uses a 1-bit power amplifier controlled by delta-sigma modulation (DSM—converting signals into rapid on-off pulses). Phase angles are encoded through edge-selection (the timing of transitions) rather than using CORDIC (an algorithm that converts angles but adds distortion). The 1-bit design naturally maintains signal linearity without distortion-correction circuits while avoiding the power losses of switched-capacitor amplifiers.
key_novelty: Edge-selection-based phase modulation in a 1-bit DSM power amplifier replaces CORDIC, achieving signal linearity without digital pre-distortion.
contributions: CORDIC-less digital polar transmitter with 1-bit DSM PA
Intrinsically linear 1-bit PA architecture avoiding switch-capacitor losses
primary_theme: CORDIC-less polar transmitter with 1-bit DSM PA
